| Expiry                                                                                       | The default validity of the [delivery settings](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/delivery/index.md), from the message's final status. An expired notification is not sent. |
| ESME deleted                                                                                 | Its notifications are dropped.                                                                                                                                                             |

Notifications are delivered at least once. The SIM answer and the receipt of a message share its `receipted_message_id`, and differ by the message type of `esm_class`.

### Delivery receipts

A receipt is an SMSC Delivery Receipt (§2.11, §4.6.1, Appendix B):

| Field                                                 | Value                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `source_addr_ton`, `source_addr_npi`, `source_addr`   | The destination of the message, as submitted. |
| `dest_addr_ton`, `dest_addr_npi`, `destination_addr`  | The source of the message, as submitted.      |
| `esm_class`                                           | `0x04`, SMSC Delivery Receipt.                |
| `protocol_id`, `priority_flag`, `registered_delivery` | `0`.                                          |
| `data_coding`                                         | `0x01`, IA5. **Convention**.                  |
| `short_message`                                       | The receipt text.                             |
| `receipted_message_id` (`0x001E`)                     | The `message_id`.                             |
| `message_state` (`0x0427`)                            | See the table below.                          |
| `user_message_reference` (`0x0204`)                   | That of the `submit_sm`, when present.        |

The text follows the example format of Appendix B:

```
id:42 sub:001 dlvrd:001 submit date:2610281430 done date:2610281431 stat:DELIVRD err:000 text:
```

| Field         | Value                                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | The `message_id`, not padded.                                                                                               |
| `sub`         | `001`.                                                                                                                      |
| `dlvrd`       | `001` for a delivered message, else `000`.                                                                                  |
| `submit date` | When the SMSC received the message, `YYMMDDhhmm`, UTC.                                                                      |
| `done date`   | When the message reached its final status, `YYMMDDhhmm`, UTC. For a replaced message, when it was replaced. **Convention**. |
| `stat`, `err` | See the table below.                                                                                                        |
| `text`        | Empty.                                                                                                                      |

| Message status | `stat`    | `message_state` (§5.2.28) | `err`                                                         |
| -------------- | --------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `delivered`    | `DELIVRD` | `2`                       | `000`                                                         |
| `expired`      | `EXPIRED` | `3`                       | `070`, TP-Status `0x46`                                       |
| `replaced`     | `DELETED` | `4`                       | `002`, TP-Status `0x02`                                       |
| `failed`       | `UNDELIV` | `5`                       | The TP-Status of the failure, such as `066`, TP-Status `0x42` |

`err` is the TP-Status (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.15), in decimal. **Convention**. `network_error_code` is not sent.

### SIM answers

The SIM answer is the TP-User-Data of the SMS-DELIVER-REPORT of the last delivery attempt (TS 23.040 §9.2.2.1a), from the RP-ACK, or from the RP-ERROR of an SM delivery failure. For a (U)SIM data download message, it is the SIM's Response Packet (TS 31.115 §4.4; TS 31.111 §7.1.1.1).

It is sent when `registered_delivery` bits 3-2 are `10` or `11`, for any `protocol_id`, as an SME Manual/User Acknowledgement (§2.11). **Convention**.

No SIM answer is sent for a replaced message, or when the SMS-DELIVER-REPORT has no TP-User-Data.

| Field                    | Value                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Addresses                | As in a receipt.                                                                                                                                           |
| `esm_class` message type | `0100`, SME Manual/User Acknowledgement. **Convention**.                                                                                                   |
| `esm_class` UDHI         | `1` when the report has TP-UDHI, or when the message's TP-PID is `0x7F` and the user data starts with a valid user data header (TS 31.115 §4.1). Else `0`. |
| `esm_class`, typical     | `0x50`                                                                                                                                                     |
| `protocol_id`            | The report's TP-PID, else the message's.                                                                                                                   |
| `data_coding`            | See the table below.                                                                                                                                       |
| `short_message`          | The TP-User-Data, its user data header included, such as `027100…`.                                                                                        |
| `receipted_message_id`   | The `message_id`. **Convention**: §5.3.2.12 defines it for receipts.                                                                                       |
| `message_state`          | Absent.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `user_message_reference` | That of the `submit_sm`, when present.                                                                                                                     |

| Report TP-DCS                                 | `data_coding`                                                                      | `short_message`         |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| GSM 7-bit, or no TP-DCS (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.27) | `0x00`                                                                             | Septets, one per octet. |
| UCS2                                          | `0x08`                                                                             | The octets.             |
| 8-bit                                         | That of the `submit_sm` when it is `0x02`, `0x04` or `0xF4` to `0xF7`, else `0x04` | The octets.             |

A SIM that rejects a (U)SIM data download message answers with an RP-ERROR whose TP-Failure-Cause is `0xD5`, (U)SIM data download error. The message fails at once with TP-Status `0x42`: the ESME gets the SIM answer, then the receipt `stat:UNDELIV err:066`.

## `command_status` values

Values the SMSC sends (§5.1.3):

| `command_status`        | Value        | Sent in          | When                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------- | ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ESME_ROK`              | `0x00000000` | Any response     | Success.                                                                                                     |
| `ESME_RINVMSGLEN`       | `0x00000001` | `submit_sm_resp` | `sm_length`, or user data longer than one TPDU.                                                              |
| `ESME_RINVCMDLEN`       | `0x00000002` | `generic_nack`   | `command_length`, or a body of the wrong length.                                                             |
| `ESME_RINVCMDID`        | `0x00000003` | `generic_nack`   | Unsupported or undefined `command_id`.                                                                       |
| `ESME_RINVBNDSTS`       | `0x00000004` | Response         | A request that the session state does not allow.                                                             |
| `ESME_RALYBND`          | `0x00000005` | Bind response    | A bind in a bound state.                                                                                     |
| `ESME_RSYSERR`          | `0x00000008` | `submit_sm_resp` | The message could not be stored or encoded.                                                                  |
| `ESME_RINVSRCADR`       | `0x0000000A` | `submit_sm_resp` | `source_addr`.                                                                                               |
| `ESME_RINVDSTADR`       | `0x0000000B` | `submit_sm_resp` | `destination_addr`.                                                                                          |
| `ESME_RBINDFAIL`        | `0x0000000D` | Bind response    | Any refused bind.                                                                                            |
| `ESME_RINVSUBREP`       | `0x00000042` | `submit_sm_resp` | `replace_if_present_flag` `1`.                                                                               |
| `ESME_RINVESMCLASS`     | `0x00000043` | `submit_sm_resp` | `esm_class`.                                                                                                 |
| `ESME_RSUBMITFAIL`      | `0x00000045` | `submit_sm_resp` | `data_coding`, `protocol_id`, the user data header, or GSM 7-bit, IA5 or UCS2 user data.                     |
| `ESME_RINVSRCTON`       | `0x00000048` | `submit_sm_resp` | `source_addr_ton`.                                                                                           |
| `ESME_RINVSRCNPI`       | `0x00000049` | `submit_sm_resp` | `source_addr_npi`.                                                                                           |
| `ESME_RINVDSTTON`       | `0x00000050` | `submit_sm_resp` | `dest_addr_ton`.                                                                                             |
| `ESME_RINVDSTNPI`       | `0x00000051` | `submit_sm_resp` | `dest_addr_npi`.                                                                                             |
| `ESME_RTHROTTLED`       | `0x00000058` | `submit_sm_resp` | Inbound window full.                                                                                         |
| `ESME_RINVSCHED`        | `0x00000061` | `submit_sm_resp` | `schedule_delivery_time`.                                                                                    |
| `ESME_RINVEXPIRY`       | `0x00000062` | `submit_sm_resp` | `validity_period`.                                                                                           |
| `ESME_RINVDFTMSGID`     | `0x00000063` | `submit_sm_resp` | `sm_default_msg_id`.                                                                                         |
| `ESME_RINVOPTPARSTREAM` | `0x000000C0` | Response         | Optional parameters that do not decode.                                                                      |
| `ESME_ROPTPARNOTALLWD`  | `0x000000C1` | `submit_sm_resp` | `short_message` with `message_payload`; `sar_*` or ports with UDHI.                                          |
| `ESME_RINVPARLEN`       | `0x000000C2` | Response         | A field over its maximum length, or a TLV of the wrong length.                                               |
| `ESME_RINVOPTPARAMVAL`  | `0x000000C4` | `submit_sm_resp` | `sar_*` values; `dest_addr_subunit` against `data_coding`; a TLV that should be a C-Octet String and is not. |
| `ESME_RUNKNOWNERR`      | `0x000000FF` | `generic_nack`   | Invalid `sequence_number`.                                                                                   |

An error response has no body (§4.1.2, §4.1.4, §4.4.2), except `bind_transceiver_resp`, which carries `system_id` (Table 4-6). The SMSC logs the reason of a refused `submit_sm` at level `debug`, with the `system_id`.

Values the SMSC acts on in `deliver_sm_resp`: see [Notifications](#notifications).

## Conventions

Behaviours that SMPP 3.4 does not define:

| Behaviour                                                                                | Where                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TLS from the first octet.                                                                | [Transport](#transport)                                                 |
| A maximum `command_length` of 68 KiB.                                                    | [Transport](#transport)                                                 |
| `data_coding` `0x00` is the GSM 7-bit default alphabet, unpacked.                        | [`data_coding`](#data_coding)                                           |
| `data_coding` `0x02` or `0x04` with `protocol_id` `0x7F` becomes TP-DCS `0xF6`, class 2. | [`data_coding`](#data_coding)                                           |
| A replace type `protocol_id` replaces only messages of the same ESME.                    | [`protocol_id`](#protocol_id)                                           |
| A two-digit year is within 49 years before and 50 years after the current year.          | [Validity and scheduling](#validity-and-scheduling)                     |
| A missing `source_port` or `destination_port` is port 0.                                 | [User data and optional parameters](#user-data-and-optional-parameters) |
| Notifications go to a receiving session of the ESME that submitted the message.          | [Notifications](#notifications)                                         |
| Receipts use `data_coding` `0x01`.                                                       | [Delivery receipts](#delivery-receipts)                                 |
| A replaced message's receipt is `DELETED`, with `done date` the replacement time.        | [Delivery receipts](#delivery-receipts)                                 |
| Receipt `err` is the TP-Status in decimal.                                               | [Delivery receipts](#delivery-receipts)                                 |
| The SIM's answer is an SME Manual/User Acknowledgement, with `receipted_message_id`.     | [SIM answers](#sim-answers)                                             |

## Not supported

- SMPP 3.3 and earlier, and SMPP 5.0.
- `query_sm`, `replace_sm`, `cancel_sm`, `submit_multi`, `data_sm`, `alert_notification` and `outbind`.
- Messages from phones to ESMEs, such as a Response Packet that the SIM sends in an SMS-SUBMIT (TS 31.115 §4.2).
- Splitting user data longer than one TPDU.
- Scheduled delivery, the datagram and transaction modes, SME delivery acknowledgements and intermediate notifications.
- The PROXY protocol.

# API

## Authentication

Requests send a token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

The token is either:

- an access token, from [log in](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/auth/#log-in) or [refresh the access token](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/auth/#refresh-the-access-token), valid for 15 minutes;
- an [API token](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/users/#create-an-api-token), which starts with `ellasmsc_`.

These paths take no token: `GET /api/v1/livez`, `GET /api/v1/readyz`, `GET /api/v1/status`, `GET /api/v1/metrics`, `GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml`, `POST /api/v1/init`, and `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, `/refresh` and `/logout`.

### Roles

| Role            | `role_id` | Allows                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Admin           | `1`       | Everything.                                                                                                                                 |
| Read Only       | `2`       | Reading messages without their content, Diameter, operator, delivery and retention settings, and ESMEs.                                     |
| Network Manager | `3`       | Read Only, plus reading message content, sending messages, updating operator, delivery and retention settings, and managing Diameter peers. |
| Submitter       | `4`       | Sending messages, and reading the messages it sent, their content included.                                                                 |

An API token has the role of its user, but cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users or [ESMEs](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md).

Only an Admin manages ESMEs. An [ESME](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md) binds over SMPP with the role of its user.

## Responses

Ella SMSC's API responses are JSON objects. A successful response carries a `result`:

```
{
    "result": "Result content"
}
```

A failed response carries an `error`:

```
{
    "error": "Error message"
}
```

`GET /api/v1/livez` and `GET /api/v1/readyz` answer 204 with no body when they succeed. `GET /api/v1/metrics` returns text in the [Prometheus exposition format](https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exposition_formats/#text-format-details), `GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml` returns YAML, and unknown paths and methods answer in plain text.

Times are RFC 3339, in UTC.

## OpenAPI Specification

The full API is described by an [OpenAPI 3.1](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0) specification embedded in the binary. Fetch it from any running Ella SMSC instance:

```
GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml
```

## Status codes

- 200 - Success.
- 201 - Created.
- 204 - No content.
- 400 - Bad request.
- 401 - Missing, invalid or expired token.
- 403 - Not allowed for the role or the token.
- 404 - Not found.
- 405 - Method not allowed.
- 409 - Conflict.
- 429 - Too many requests. `Retry-After` is the seconds to wait.
- 500 - Internal server error.
- 503 - Not ready. See [Check readiness](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/status/#check-readiness).

# Authentication

## Log In

This path returns an access token, and sets the session cookie, `smsc_session`, or `__Host-smsc_session` over TLS. The session lasts 30 days, and a user has at most 10.

| Method | Path                 |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/auth/login` |

### Request Body

| Field      | Type   | Required | Description                 |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------- |
| `email`    | string | Yes      | Email address, in any case. |
| `password` | string | Yes      | Password.                   |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                                                              |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401` | Wrong email or password.                                                                                                                 |
| `429` | More than 20 attempts in a minute from the client address, or its IPv6 /64; or more than 100 wrong passwords in an hour for the account. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Login successful",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}
```

## Refresh the Access Token

This path returns a new access token for the session of the cookie.

| Method | Path                   |
| ------ | ---------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/auth/refresh` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                       |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401` | No session, or the session ended. The response clears the cookie. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}
```

## Log Out

This path ends the session of the cookie, and its access tokens, and clears the cookie.

| Method | Path                  |
| ------ | --------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/auth/logout` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                |
| ----- | -------------------------- |
| `204` | Logged out, or no session. |

# Delivery

The delivery settings set how long the SMSC attempts delivery of a message, and when it retries a failed delivery. The [retention](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/retention/index.md) sets how long it keeps a message afterwards.

## Get the Delivery Settings

This path returns the delivery settings.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/delivery` |

### Response Fields

| Field                      | Type  | Description                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default_validity_seconds` | int   | How long delivery of a message without its own validity period is attempted, in seconds. The same applies to status reports. |
| `retry_intervals_seconds`  | array | Wait before each retry, in seconds. The last interval repeats. Empty: a failed delivery is not retried.                      |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "default_validity_seconds": 604800,
        "retry_intervals_seconds": [60, 300, 900, 3600]
    }
}
```

## Update the Delivery Settings

This path replaces the delivery settings. The new validity applies to the messages received afterwards; the new intervals, to the next retries.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/delivery` |

### Request Body

| Field                      | Type  | Required | Description                    |
| -------------------------- | ----- | -------- | ------------------------------ |
| `default_validity_seconds` | int   | Yes      | `1` to `315360000` (10 years). |
| `retry_intervals_seconds`  | array | Yes      | Each at least 1.               |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "default_validity_seconds": 86400,
    "retry_intervals_seconds": [60, 300]
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "default_validity_seconds": 86400,
        "retry_intervals_seconds": [60, 300]
    }
}
```

# Diameter

Configured peers are the Diameter agents that the SMSC connects to, and their routes. Creating, updating and deleting them requires Network Manager or Admin.

## Get the Diameter Status

This path returns the Diameter identity of the SMSC, its peers, and its routes.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/diameter` |

### Response Fields

| Field                  | Type    | Description                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`                 | string  | Origin-Host of the SMSC.                                                                  |
| `realm`                | string  | Origin-Realm of the SMSC.                                                                 |
| `peers`                | array   | Connected and configured peers.                                                           |
| `peers[].id`           | int     | ID of a configured peer.                                                                  |
| `peers[].configured`   | boolean | Whether the peer is configured.                                                           |
| `peers[].host`         | string  | Origin-Host of the peer.                                                                  |
| `peers[].realm`        | string  | Origin-Realm of the peer.                                                                 |
| `peers[].address`      | string  | Remote address of the connection.                                                         |
| `peers[].state`        | string  | `down`, `connecting`, `open`, `suspect`, `reopen` or `closing`.                           |
| `peers[].applications` | array   | Applications the peer supports: `s6c`, `sgd`.                                             |
| `peers[].since`        | string  | Time of the last state change.                                                            |
| `peers[].error`        | string  | Last connection error of a configured peer.                                               |
| `routes`               | array   | The `s6c` route to the HSS, then the routes of the configured peers, default routes last. |
| `routes[].realm`       | string  | Destination-Realm. Empty for a default route.                                             |
| `routes[].default`     | boolean | Whether the route is a default route.                                                     |
| `routes[].application` | string  | `s6c` or `sgd`.                                                                           |
| `routes[].peers`       | array   | Hosts of the open peers of the route.                                                     |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "host": "smsc.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "peers": [
            {
                "configured": false,
                "host": "core.example.org",
                "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "address": "127.0.0.1",
                "state": "open",
                "applications": ["sgd", "s6c"],
                "since": "2026-10-27T18:46:07.330Z"
            },
            {
                "id": 1,
                "configured": true,
                "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
                "realm": "ipx.example.net",
                "address": "192.0.2.10",
                "state": "open",
                "applications": ["sgd", "s6c"],
                "since": "2026-10-27T18:47:12.004Z"
            }
        ],
        "routes": [
            {
                "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "default": false,
                "application": "s6c",
                "peers": ["core.example.org"]
            },
            {
                "realm": "",
                "default": true,
                "application": "sgd",
                "peers": ["dea1.ipx.example.net"]
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## List Peers

| Method | Path                     |
| ------ | ------------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/diameter/peers` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 1,
                "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
                "addresses": ["192.0.2.10", "198.51.100.10"],
                "port": 3868,
                "routes": [
                    { "default": true, "application": "sgd", "priority": 0 }
                ],
                "status": {
                    "state": "open",
                    "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
                    "realm": "ipx.example.net",
                    "since": "2026-10-27T18:47:12.004Z"
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Create a Peer

| Method | Path                     |
| ------ | ------------------------ |
| POST   | `/api/v1/diameter/peers` |

### Request Body

| Field                  | Type    | Required         | Description                                                                                           |
| ---------------------- | ------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`                 | string  | No               | Origin-Host the peer must give. Empty accepts any.                                                    |
| `addresses`            | array   | Yes              | IP addresses of the peer. A peer with a `host` must connect from one of them.                         |
| `port`                 | int     | No               | Default `3868`.                                                                                       |
| `routes`               | array   | No               | Routes of the peer.                                                                                   |
| `routes[].realm`       | string  | Unless `default` | Destination-Realm, e.g. `epc.mnc002.mcc208.3gppnetwork.org`.                                          |
| `routes[].default`     | boolean | No               | Default route: every realm without another route, except the SMSC's own. `sgd` only, without `realm`. |
| `routes[].application` | string  | Yes              | `sgd` or `s6c`. An `s6c` route takes the SMSC's own realm.                                            |
| `routes[].priority`    | int     | No               | Lowest first; equal priorities share the load. Default `0`.                                           |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
    "addresses": ["192.0.2.10", "198.51.100.10"],
    "routes": [
        { "default": true, "application": "sgd" },
        { "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org", "application": "s6c" }
    ]
}
```

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                             |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `201` | The peer, with its `id`.                                                                |
| `400` | Invalid peer.                                                                           |
| `409` | `host` is another peer's or the SMSC's, or two peers without a `host` share an address. |

## Get a Peer

| Method | Path                          |
| ------ | ----------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}` |

### Response Fields

The fields of the request body, plus:

| Field          | Type   | Description                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`           | int    | ID of the peer.                                                                                              |
| `status`       | object | Connection to the peer. Absent until the SMSC applies the peer, and from the responses to create and update. |
| `status.state` | string | `down`, `connecting`, `open`, `suspect`, `reopen` or `closing`.                                              |
| `status.host`  | string | Origin-Host the peer gave.                                                                                   |
| `status.realm` | string | Origin-Realm the peer gave.                                                                                  |
| `status.since` | string | Time of the last state change.                                                                               |
| `status.error` | string | Last connection error.                                                                                       |

## Update a Peer

The request body is that of [Create a Peer](#create-a-peer). A change of `host`, `addresses` or `port` reconnects.

| Method | Path                          |
| ------ | ----------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}` |

## Delete a Peer

| Method | Path                          |
| ------ | ----------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}` |

# ESMEs

An ESME account is what an External Short Message Entity, such as an OTA platform, binds to the [SMPP listener](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md) with, with at most 4 sessions at once. It acts as its user: the messages it submits are the user's, and the user's role decides which binds it may make. See [Binds](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/#binds).

Reading ESMEs requires Admin, Read Only or Network Manager. Creating, updating and deleting them requires Admin, and an access token: an API token gets `403`.

## List ESMEs

| Method | Path            |
| ------ | --------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/esmes` |

### Response Fields

| Field                       | Type   | Description                                 |
| --------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `system_id`                 | string | The `system_id` the ESME binds with.        |
| `user`                      | string | Email of the user the ESME acts as.         |
| `allowed_networks`          | array  | IP prefixes the ESME may bind from.         |
| `created_at`                | string | Time the ESME was created.                  |
| `sessions`                  | array  | Bound sessions, oldest first.               |
| `sessions[].bind_type`      | string | `transmitter`, `receiver` or `transceiver`. |
| `sessions[].remote_address` | string | Address and port of the client.             |
| `sessions[].bound_at`       | string | Time of the bind.                           |

The password is never returned.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "system_id": "ota",
                "user": "ota@example.com",
                "allowed_networks": ["10.1.0.0/24"],
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:40:02.118Z",
                "sessions": [
                    {
                        "bind_type": "transceiver",
                        "remote_address": "10.1.0.5:40312",
                        "bound_at": "2026-10-27T18:41:55.906Z"
                    }
                ]
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Create an ESME

At most 50 ESMEs. Without a `password`, the SMSC generates one of 8 letters and digits, and returns it as `password` in this response only.

| Method | Path            |
| ------ | --------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/esmes` |

### Request Body

| Field              | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `system_id`        | string | Yes      | 1 to 15 printable ASCII characters (SMPP 3.4 §4.1.1).                                                      |
| `user`             | string | Yes      | Email of an existing user, the user the ESME acts as.                                                      |
| `password`         | string | No       | 1 to 8 printable ASCII characters (SMPP 3.4 §4.1.1). Default: generated.                                   |
| `allowed_networks` | array  | No       | IP prefixes, such as `10.1.0.0/24` or `2001:db8::/64`, at most 50. Default: none, which allows no address. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "system_id": "ota",
    "user": "ota@example.com",
    "allowed_networks": ["10.1.0.0/24"]
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "system_id": "ota",
        "user": "ota@example.com",
        "allowed_networks": ["10.1.0.0/24"],
        "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:40:02.118Z",
        "sessions": [],
        "password": "q7Rk2LxW"
    }
}
```

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                  |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `201` | The ESME, with the generated `password` when none was given. |
| `400` | Invalid field, no user with the email, or 50 ESMEs exist.    |
| `409` | An ESME has the `system_id`.                                 |

## Get an ESME

| Method | Path                        |
| ------ | --------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/esmes/{system_id}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name        | Type   | Description                               |
| ----------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `system_id` | string | The `system_id` of the ESME, URL-encoded. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                   |
| ----- | ----------------------------- |
| `404` | No ESME has this `system_id`. |

## Update an ESME

This path replaces the allowed networks of an ESME, and its password when one is given, and closes its sessions, which bind again under the new settings. The `system_id` and the user cannot be changed.

| Method | Path                        |
| ------ | --------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/esmes/{system_id}` |

### Request Body

| Field              | Type   | Required | Description                                                        |
| ------------------ | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `password`         | string | No       | 1 to 8 printable ASCII characters. Without it, the password stays. |
| `allowed_networks` | array  | Yes      | As in [Create an ESME](#create-an-esme).                           |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                   |
| ----- | ----------------------------- |
| `200` | The ESME.                     |
| `400` | Invalid field.                |
| `404` | No ESME has this `system_id`. |

## Delete an ESME

This path deletes an ESME, closes its sessions, and drops the receipts and SIM answers not yet sent to it. Its messages stay, as its user's. Deleting the user deletes its ESMEs.

| Method | Path                        |
| ------ | --------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/esmes/{system_id}` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "ESME deleted successfully"
    }
}
```

# Initialize

## Initialize Ella SMSC

This path creates the first user, an Admin, and logs it in.

| Method | Path           |
| ------ | -------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/init` |

### Request Body

| Field      | Type   | Required | Description    |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | -------------- |
| `email`    | string | Yes      | Email address. |
| `password` | string | Yes      | 8 to 72 bytes. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `201` | Created.                                   |
| `403` | A user exists.                             |
| `429` | Too many attempts from the client address. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "email": "admin@example.com",
    "password": "correct horse"
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "System initialized successfully",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}
```

# Messages

A message is a short message the SMSC received, from a phone, from the API, or from an ESME over [SMPP](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md), with its delivery status and the status reports the SMSC returned to the phone that sent it. A text longer than one short message is split into parts, one message each.

Responses carry no content. [Get the content of a message](#get-the-content-of-a-message) returns it, and logs an audit event.

## Create a Message

This path submits a text message, or a binary message, to a phone. It returns one message per part.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| POST   | `/api/v1/messages` |

### Request Body

| Field                        | Type   | Required                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | ------ | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `from`                       | string | Yes                        | Shown to the recipient as the sender. An E.164 number with `+`, or a name of 1 to 11 ASCII letters and digits, with single spaces between words, that is not all digits, such as `EllaSMSC`. A value without `+` is a name, delivered as given.                                                                                                                                        |
| `to`                         | string | Yes                        | E.164 number with `+` of the recipient.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `text`                       | string | One of `text` and `binary` | Not empty. GSM-7 if every character is in the GSM 7-bit default alphabet or its extension table, else UCS-2. Up to 255 parts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `binary`                     | object | One of `text` and `binary` | TPDU parameters of one short message, delivered unchanged.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `binary.protocol_identifier` | int    | No                         | TP-PID (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.9), `0` to `255`. Default `0`. Not `32` to `62`, telematic interworking. `65` to `71`, replace types 1 to 7, replace the pending message of the same type from the same `from`, submitted by the same user; never a message from a phone or an ESME. `72`, device triggering, needs an application port addressing information element in `user_data_header`. |
| `binary.data_coding_scheme`  | int    | Yes                        | TP-DCS (TS 23.038 §4), `0` to `255`. Not a GSM 7-bit, UCS2 or reserved coding. Message class 2 when `protocol_identifier` is `124`, ANSI-136 R-DATA, or `127`, (U)SIM data download.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `binary.user_data_header`    | string | No                         | TP-UDH (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24) in hexadecimal, its length octet included.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `binary.user_data`           | string | Yes                        | TP-UD after the header, in hexadecimal. May be empty. At most 140 octets with `user_data_header`. Not split into parts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `validity_seconds`           | int    | No                         | How long delivery is attempted, `1` to `315360000` (10 years). Default: the default validity of the [delivery settings](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/delivery/index.md).                                                                                                                                                                                           |

A message from the API never asks for status reports.

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                                                                            |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `400` | A field is missing or invalid, both or neither of `text` and `binary`, the text needs more than 255 parts, or the binary user data is over 140 octets. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "from": "+15550001000",
    "to": "+15551230002",
    "text": "Your code is 1234"
}
```

### Sample Request (Binary)

```
{
    "from": "+15550001000",
    "to": "+15551230002",
    "binary": {
        "protocol_identifier": 127,
        "data_coding_scheme": 246,
        "user_data_header": "027000",
        "user_data": "0011223344"
    }
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 1,
                "from": "+15550001000",
                "to": "+15551230002",
                "encoding": "gsm7",
                "status": "pending",
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:44:19.436Z",
                "updated_at": "2026-10-27T18:44:19.436Z",
                "expires_at": "2026-11-03T18:44:19.436Z",
                "next_attempt_at": "2026-10-27T18:44:19.436Z",
                "status_report": {
                    "requested": false,
                    "reports": []
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## List Messages

This path returns the list of messages, most recent first. For a Submitter, only the messages it sent.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/messages` |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed                                                                                      | Description                                                                                                          |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `to`       | query | str  |         | 1 to 15 digits, after an optional `+`                                                        | Recipient: the numbers that contain these digits. `+1555123` and `1555123` match `+15551230002`, and so does `0002`. |
| `from`     | query | str  |         | 1 to 15 digits, after an optional `+`, or a name as in [Create a Message](#create-a-message) | Sender: the numbers that contain these digits, or the name, in any case.                                             |
| `status`   | query | str  |         | `pending`, `delivered`, `failed`, `expired`, `replaced`                                      | Status.                                                                                                              |
| `start`    | query | str  |         | RFC 3339 time                                                                                | Created at or after.                                                                                                 |
| `end`      | query | str  |         | RFC 3339 time, not before `start`                                                            | Created before.                                                                                                      |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`                                                                                       | 1-based page index.                                                                                                  |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1…100`                                                                                      | Number of items per page.                                                                                            |

### Response Fields

| Field                                     | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                                      | int     | Message identifier.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `from`                                    | string  | Sender: the MSISDN of the phone, an E.164 number with `+`, the `from` of the API request, or the `source_addr` of the `submit_sm`, with `+` when international.                                         |
| `to`                                      | string  | Recipient, an E.164 number with `+`.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `encoding`                                | string  | `gsm7`, `ucs2` or `binary`.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `concatenation`                           | object  | Present for a part of a longer message.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `concatenation.reference`                 | int     | Reference shared by the parts of the message.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `concatenation.part`                      | int     | Number of this part, from 1.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `concatenation.total`                     | int     | Number of parts.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `status`                                  | string  | `pending`; `delivered`; `failed`; `expired`, when its validity period ended before its delivery; or `replaced`, by a later message from the same sender, of the same replace type, before its delivery. |
| `created_at`                              | string  | Time the SMSC received the message.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `updated_at`                              | string  | Time of the last change.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `expires_at`                              | string  | End of the validity period.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `next_attempt_at`                         | string  | Time of the next delivery attempt. Present while `pending`.                                                                                                                                             |
| `status_report`                           | object  | Status reports on the message.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `status_report.requested`                 | boolean | Whether the phone that sent the message asked for status reports.                                                                                                                                       |
| `status_report.reports`                   | array   | Status reports the SMSC returned to that phone, oldest first.                                                                                                                                           |
| `status_report.reports[].id`              | int     | Status report identifier.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `status_report.reports[].tp_status`       | int     | TP-Status the report gives (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.15).                                                                                                                                                       |
| `status_report.reports[].tp_status_name`  | string  | Meaning of `tp_status`, e.g. `received`, `replaced`, `no_response`, `validity_period_expired`.                                                                                                          |
| `status_report.reports[].status`          | string  | Delivery of the report to the phone: `pending`, `delivered`, `failed` or `expired`.                                                                                                                     |
| `status_report.reports[].created_at`      | string  | Time the SMSC made the report.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `status_report.reports[].updated_at`      | string  | Time of the last change.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `status_report.reports[].expires_at`      | string  | End of the report's validity period.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `status_report.reports[].next_attempt_at` | string  | Time of the next delivery attempt of the report. Present while `pending`.                                                                                                                               |
| `submitted_by`                            | string  | Email of the user that sent the message over the API, or of the user of the ESME that sent it over SMPP. Absent for a message from a phone.                                                             |
| `system_id`                               | string  | `system_id` of the [ESME](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md) that sent the message over SMPP. Absent for other messages, and once the ESME is deleted.                    |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 4,
                "from": "+15550001000",
                "to": "+15551230001",
                "encoding": "gsm7",
                "concatenation": {
                    "reference": 74,
                    "part": 2,
                    "total": 2
                },
                "status": "pending",
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:53:37.120Z",
                "updated_at": "2026-10-27T18:54:07.151Z",
                "expires_at": "2026-11-03T18:53:37.120Z",
                "next_attempt_at": "2026-10-27T18:55:07.151Z",
                "status_report": {
                    "requested": false,
                    "reports": []
                }
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 1,
        "total_count": 3
    }
}
```

## Get a Message

This path returns a specific message. For a Submitter, a message it did not send is not found.

| Method | Path                    |
| ------ | ----------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/messages/{id}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type | Description         |
| ---- | ---- | ------------------- |
| `id` | int  | Message identifier. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                     |
| ----- | ------------------------------- |
| `404` | No message has this identifier. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "id": 1,
        "from": "+15551230001",
        "to": "+15551230002",
        "encoding": "gsm7",
        "status": "delivered",
        "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:07.350Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.355Z",
        "expires_at": "2026-11-03T18:46:07.350Z",
        "status_report": {
            "requested": true,
            "reports": [
                {
                    "id": 2,
                    "tp_status": 0,
                    "tp_status_name": "received",
                    "status": "delivered",
                    "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.355Z",
                    "updated_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.356Z",
                    "expires_at": "2026-11-03T18:46:10.355Z"
                }
            ]
        }
    }
}
```

## Get the Content of a Message

This path returns the content of a message, and logs an audit event `read_message_content` with the email of the caller. For a Submitter, a message it did not send is not found. A Read Only user cannot read content.

| Method | Path                            |
| ------ | ------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/messages/{id}/content` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type | Description         |
| ---- | ---- | ------------------- |
| `id` | int  | Message identifier. |

### Response Fields

| Field                                   | Type   | Description                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`                                  | string | Text of the part. Absent for a binary message.                                                                                  |
| `binary`                                | object | TPDU parameters of a binary message.                                                                                            |
| `binary.protocol_identifier`            | int    | TP-PID.                                                                                                                         |
| `binary.data_coding_scheme`             | int    | TP-DCS.                                                                                                                         |
| `binary.user_data_header`               | string | TP-UDH in hexadecimal, its length octet included. Absent when there is none.                                                    |
| `binary.user_data`                      | string | TP-UD after the header, in hexadecimal.                                                                                         |
| `deliver_reports`                       | array  | SMS-DELIVER-REPORTs (TS 23.040 §9.2.2.1a) the serving nodes passed on, oldest first. Absent when there are none.                |
| `deliver_reports[].attempt_id`          | int    | [Delivery attempt](#list-delivery-attempts) of the report: in the RP-ACK when its `outcome` is `success`, else in the RP-ERROR. |
| `deliver_reports[].tpdu`                | string | The report in hexadecimal. The other `deliver_reports[]` fields are absent when it does not decode.                             |
| `deliver_reports[].protocol_identifier` | int    | TP-PID, when present.                                                                                                           |
| `deliver_reports[].data_coding_scheme`  | int    | TP-DCS, when present.                                                                                                           |
| `deliver_reports[].user_data_header`    | string | TP-UDH in hexadecimal, when present.                                                                                            |
| `deliver_reports[].user_data`           | string | TP-UD after the header, in hexadecimal, when present.                                                                           |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                     |
| ----- | ------------------------------- |
| `404` | No message has this identifier. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "text": "Your code is 1234"
    }
}
```

### Sample Response (Binary)

```
{
    "result": {
        "binary": {
            "protocol_identifier": 127,
            "data_coding_scheme": 246,
            "user_data_header": "027000",
            "user_data": "0011223344"
        },
        "deliver_reports": [
            {
                "attempt_id": 2,
                "tpdu": "00077ff602cafe",
                "protocol_identifier": 127,
                "data_coding_scheme": 246,
                "user_data": "cafe"
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## List Delivery Attempts

This path returns the routing and delivery attempts of a message, oldest first. For a Submitter, a message it did not send is not found.

| Method | Path                             |
| ------ | -------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/messages/{id}/attempts` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type | Description         |
| ---- | ---- | ------------------- |
| `id` | int  | Message identifier. |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed | Description               |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | ------- | ------------------------- |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`  | 1-based page index.       |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1…100` | Number of items per page. |

### Response Fields

| Field                     | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                      | int    | Attempt identifier.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `started_at`              | string | Start of the attempt.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `completed_at`            | string | End of the attempt.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `step`                    | string | `routing`: a routing lookup at the HSS, over S6c. `delivery`: a delivery to a serving node, over SGd.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `node`                    | string | Host of the HSS that answered the routing lookup, or of the serving node.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `node_type`               | string | Type of the serving node: `mme`, `sgsn`, `ip_sm_gw`, `smsf_3gpp` or `smsf_non_3gpp`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `outcome`                 | string | `success`; `no_hss`, no HSS connected; `unreachable`, the serving node not connected; `timeout`, no answer in time; the error the node gave: `user_unknown`, `absent_user`, `user_busy_for_mt_sms`, `facility_not_supported`, `illegal_user`, `illegal_equipment`, `sm_delivery_failure`, `service_not_subscribed`, `service_barred`, `mwd_list_full`; `diameter_error`, another error answer; or `error`. |
| `result_code`             | int    | Result-Code or Experimental-Result-Code of the answer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `vendor_id`               | int    | Vendor-Id of an Experimental-Result-Code.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `failure_cause`           | string | SM-Delivery-Failure-Cause of an `sm_delivery_failure`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `tp_failure_cause`        | string | TP-Failure-Cause the phone gave.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `absent_user_diagnostics` | object | Why the phone is unreachable, by node: `mme`, `msc`, `sgsn`, `ip_sm_gw`, `smsf_3gpp`, `smsf_non_3gpp`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

A value the SMSC did not observe is absent.

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                     |
| ----- | ------------------------------- |
| `404` | No message has this identifier. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 1,
                "started_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:07.351Z",
                "completed_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:07.351Z",
                "step": "routing",
                "node": "core.example.org",
                "outcome": "absent_user",
                "result_code": 5550,
                "vendor_id": 10415,
                "absent_user_diagnostics": {
                    "mme": "imsi_detached"
                }
            },
            {
                "id": 2,
                "started_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.354Z",
                "completed_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.355Z",
                "step": "routing",
                "node": "core.example.org",
                "outcome": "success",
                "result_code": 2001
            },
            {
                "id": 3,
                "started_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.355Z",
                "completed_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.355Z",
                "step": "delivery",
                "node": "core.example.org",
                "node_type": "mme",
                "outcome": "success",
                "result_code": 2001
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 3
    }
}
```

# Metrics

## Get Metrics

This path returns the metrics of the SMSC in the [Prometheus exposition format](https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exposition_formats/#text-format-details), negotiated from the request's `Accept` header. See [Observability](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/observability/#metrics) for the list.

| Method | Path              |
| ------ | ----------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/metrics` |

### Sample Response

```
# HELP ellasmsc_hss_peers Open Diameter peers in the operator's realm that serve S6c, which the SMSC asks to route messages. At 0, messages to phones wait.
# TYPE ellasmsc_hss_peers gauge
ellasmsc_hss_peers 0
# HELP ellasmsc_messages_pending Short messages and status reports waiting for delivery, by type (message, status_report) and state: due (to be delivered now, or being delivered) or waiting (for a retry or for the phone to be reachable). Due messages that stay due mean the deliverer is falling behind.
# TYPE ellasmsc_messages_pending gauge
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="due",type="message"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="due",type="status_report"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="waiting",type="message"} 2
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="waiting",type="status_report"} 0
# HELP ellasmsc_messages_received_total Short messages received, one per TPDU, by origin (mobile, api) and result (accepted, rejected, error).
# TYPE ellasmsc_messages_received_total counter
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="api",result="accepted"} 2
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="api",result="error"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="mobile",result="accepted"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="mobile",result="error"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="mobile",result="rejected"} 0
```

# Operator

The operator is the PLMN of the SMSC, from which its Diameter identity derives, its service centre address, and the numbering plan that converts the numbers phones send to E.164 numbers.

## Get the Operator

This path returns the operator settings.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/operator` |

### Response Fields

| Field                            | Type   | Description                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mcc`                            | string | Mobile Country Code.                                                                                       |
| `mnc`                            | string | Mobile Network Code.                                                                                       |
| `service_centre_address`         | string | E.164 number of the SMSC, which phones have as SMSC number.                                                |
| `numbering`                      | object | Conversion of the numbers phones send to E.164 numbers.                                                    |
| `numbering.country_code`         | string | Country code, added to the numbers phones send in national format.                                         |
| `numbering.national_prefix`      | string | Prefix that phones dial before a national number, removed before the country code is added. Empty if none. |
| `numbering.international_prefix` | string | Prefix that phones dial before an international number, removed. Empty if none.                            |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "service_centre_address": "+15550000000",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011"
        }
    }
}
```

## Update the Operator

This path replaces the operator settings. A change of MCC or MNC changes the Diameter host and realm: the SMSC restarts Diameter, and its peers reconnect.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/operator` |

### Request Body

| Field                            | Type   | Required | Description                                                       |
| -------------------------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mcc`                            | string | Yes      | 3 digits.                                                         |
| `mnc`                            | string | Yes      | 2 or 3 digits.                                                    |
| `service_centre_address`         | string | Yes      | E.164 number with `+`, e.g. `+15550000000`.                       |
| `numbering`                      | object | Yes      |                                                                   |
| `numbering.country_code`         | string | Yes      | 1 to 3 digits, not starting with 0.                               |
| `numbering.national_prefix`      | string | Yes      | Up to 4 digits. Differs from `international_prefix` unless empty. |
| `numbering.international_prefix` | string | Yes      | Up to 4 digits.                                                   |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "mcc": "001",
    "mnc": "01",
    "service_centre_address": "+15550000000",
    "numbering": {
        "country_code": "1",
        "national_prefix": "1",
        "international_prefix": "011"
    }
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "service_centre_address": "+15550000000",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011"
        }
    }
}
```

# Pprof

These paths serve the [net/http/pprof](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http/pprof) API. They require Admin, and accept an API token.

## Profiling Endpoints

| Method    | Path                          | Description                                              |
| --------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/`              | An HTML page listing the available profiles.             |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/allocs`        | A sampling of all past memory allocations.               |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/cmdline`       | The command line invocation of the program.              |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/goroutine`     | Stack traces of all current goroutines.                  |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/goroutineleak` | Stack traces of all leaked goroutines.                   |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/heap`          | A sampling of memory allocations of live objects.        |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/profile`       | A CPU profile, of 30 seconds by default.                 |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/threadcreate`  | Stack traces that led to the creation of new OS threads. |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/trace`         | An execution trace, of 1 second by default.              |
| GET, POST | `/api/v1/pprof/symbol`        | Function names of program counters.                      |

### Query Parameters

| Parameter | Paths                                         | Description                                                                         |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `seconds` | `profile`, `trace`                            | Duration of the capture.                                                            |
