| `seconds` | `allocs`, `goroutine`, `heap`                 | Returns the difference of the profile over this duration.                           |
| `debug`   | `allocs`, `goroutine`, `heap`, `threadcreate` | `0`: protobuf. `1`: text. `2` (`goroutine`): stack traces in the format of a panic. |
| `gc`      | `heap`                                        | `1`: runs a garbage collection first.                                               |

# Retention

The retention sets how long the SMSC keeps a message once it has its final status: `delivered`, `failed`, `expired` or `replaced`. The SMSC then deletes it, with its status reports and delivery attempts, within the hour. It keeps a message until its status reports, too, have had their final status for that long.

## Get the Retention

This path returns the retention.

| Method | Path                         |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/messages/retention` |

### Response Fields

| Field  | Type | Description                                                         |
| ------ | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `days` | int  | Days a message is kept once it has its final status. Default: `30`. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "days": 30
    }
}
```

## Update the Retention

This path replaces the retention. It applies from the next deletion, within the hour.

| Method | Path                         |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/messages/retention` |

### Request Body

| Field  | Type | Required | Description |
| ------ | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `days` | int  | Yes      | At least 1. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "days": 7
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "days": 7
    }
}
```

# Status

## Get the Status

This path returns the version of the SMSC, and whether it is initialized.

| Method | Path             |
| ------ | ---------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/status` |

### Response Fields

| Field         | Type    | Description                                                                                                            |
| ------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `version`     | string  | Version.                                                                                                               |
| `revision`    | string  | Git commit of the build. Empty in development builds.                                                                  |
| `initialized` | boolean | Whether the first user exists. See [Initialize](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/initialize/index.md). |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "version": "v0.0.1",
        "revision": "79194832364de9583e8e659ba700c2fa9ba1e351",
        "initialized": true
    }
}
```

## Check Liveness

This path answers while the process serves HTTP.

| Method | Path            |
| ------ | --------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/livez` |

It answers `204 No Content`.

## Check Readiness

This path returns whether the SMSC can serve requests: its database answers, and it is not shutting down.

| Method | Path             |
| ------ | ---------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/readyz` |

It answers `204 No Content` when ready, and `503 Service Unavailable` otherwise:

```
{
    "error": "Not ready"
}
```

# Users

Paths under `/api/v1/users/me` act on the user of the token. The others require Admin, and an access token: an API token gets `403`.

## Get My User

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/users/me` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "email": "admin@example.com",
        "role_id": 1
    }
}
```

## Update My Password

This path ends the user's other sessions. It requires an access token.

| Method | Path                        |
| ------ | --------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/users/me/password` |

### Request Body

| Field              | Type   | Required | Description                  |
| ------------------ | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------- |
| `current_password` | string | Yes      | Current password.            |
| `password`         | string | Yes      | New password, 8 to 72 bytes. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                       |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400` | Wrong current password, or invalid new password.                                  |
| `429` | More than 100 wrong passwords in an hour for the account, counting failed logins. |

## List Users

| Method | Path            |
| ------ | --------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/users` |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed | Description               |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | ------- | ------------------------- |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`  | 1-based page index.       |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1…100` | Number of items per page. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "email": "admin@example.com",
                "role_id": 1
            },
            {
                "email": "ota@example.com",
                "role_id": 4
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 2
    }
}
```

## Create a User

At most 50 users.

| Method | Path            |
| ------ | --------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/users` |

### Request Body

| Field      | Type   | Required | Description                                                                       |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `email`    | string | Yes      | Email address. Stored in lower case.                                              |
| `password` | string | Yes      | 8 to 72 bytes.                                                                    |
| `role_id`  | int    | Yes      | `1` to `4`. See [roles](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/#roles). |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                        |
| ----- | ---------------------------------- |
| `201` | Created.                           |
| `400` | Invalid field, or 50 users exist.  |
| `409` | A user has the email, in any case. |

## Get a User

| Method | Path                    |
| ------ | ----------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/users/{email}` |

## Update a User

This path changes the role of a user, and ends its sessions and the SMPP sessions of its [ESMEs](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md). An Admin cannot change its own role.

| Method | Path                    |
| ------ | ----------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/users/{email}` |

### Request Body

| Field     | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `role_id` | int  | Yes      | `1` to `4`. |

## Update a User's Password

This path ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot update its own password here.

| Method | Path                             |
| ------ | -------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/users/{email}/password` |

### Request Body

| Field      | Type   | Required | Description    |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | -------------- |
| `password` | string | Yes      | 8 to 72 bytes. |

## Delete a User

This path deletes the user with its sessions, API tokens and [ESMEs](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md). An Admin cannot delete itself.

| Method | Path                    |
| ------ | ----------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}` |

## Create an API Token

This path returns the token, the only time it is shown. At most 12 per user. Requires an access token.

| Method | Path                               |
| ------ | ---------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/users/me/api-tokens`      |
| POST   | `/api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens` |

### Request Body

| Field        | Type   | Required | Description                                                         |
| ------------ | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`       | string | Yes      | 3 to 50 characters, unique among the user's tokens.                 |
| `expires_at` | string | No       | RFC 3339 time in the future. Without it, the token does not expire. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                        |
| ----- | ---------------------------------- |
| `201` | Created.                           |
| `400` | Invalid field, or 12 tokens exist. |
| `409` | The user has a token of that name. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "name": "OTA platform",
    "expires_at": "2027-10-27T00:00:00Z"
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "token": "ellasmsc_aB3dE5fG7hJ9_KQ4ZN2X7WJ5R3TQY6PLM2VA4CF"
    }
}
```

## List API Tokens

| Method | Path                               |
| ------ | ---------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/users/me/api-tokens`      |
| GET    | `/api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens` |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed | Description               |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | ------- | ------------------------- |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`  | 1-based page index.       |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1…100` | Number of items per page. |

### Response Fields

| Field          | Type   | Description                                                                   |
| -------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`           | string | Token identifier: the part of the token between `ellasmsc_` and the next `_`. |
| `name`         | string | Name.                                                                         |
| `created_at`   | string | Creation time.                                                                |
| `expires_at`   | string | Expiry time. Absent for a token that does not expire.                         |
| `last_used_at` | string | Time of the last use, to the minute. Absent for a token never used.           |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "aB3dE5fG7hJ9",
                "name": "OTA platform",
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:44:19.436Z",
                "expires_at": "2027-10-27T00:00:00.000Z",
                "last_used_at": "2026-10-27T19:02:00.000Z"
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}
```

## Delete an API Token

| Method | Path                                    |
| ------ | --------------------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/me/api-tokens/{id}`      |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens/{id}` |
# Explanation

# Explanation

These explanations provide context on how Ella SMSC works.

- [Architecture](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/explanation/architecture/index.md)
- [Security](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/explanation/security/index.md)

# Architecture

A Short Message Service Centre (SMSC) stores the short messages phones send, and forwards them to their recipients. Ella SMSC is a single process, with one SQLite database, one UI, one API and, when configured, an SMPP listener.

## Where Ella SMSC sits

Ella SMSC has no radio access and stores no subscribers. It relies on the core network, over Diameter:

- **The HSS**, over S6c, says where a recipient is served, and alerts the SMSC when an unreachable recipient is back.
- **The MME or SMSF**, over SGd, carries messages between the phones and the SMSC, in NAS signalling.
- **An IP-SM-GW**, over SGd, carries them for phones registered for SMS over IP.

Ella Core provides the HSS, the MME and the SMSF. For how it works with an SMSC, see Ella Core's [SMS Integration](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/explanation/sms_integration/).

Ella SMSC's Diameter host and realm derive from the operator's MCC and MNC: `smsc.node.epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org` in the realm `epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org`. Its peers connect to it, and it asks the HSSs of that realm for routing.

## Reaching other networks

A subscriber roaming on another network is served by a visited MME or SMSF that never connects to Ella SMSC. Ella SMSC reaches it through a Diameter agent it connects to, such as the edge agent of the operator or of an IPX provider. An HSS behind a DRA is reached the same way.

Each agent has routes: the realms it reaches. A default route takes every other realm, except Ella SMSC's own, so a home MME that is briefly disconnected is retried rather than sent out to the IPX. An agent is asked only for the requests of its routes: an HSS added as an agent needs an S6c route to Ella SMSC's realm.

When an agent fails with a short message in flight, Ella SMSC sends it through the next one, and the subscriber may receive it twice.

## Receiving

A phone's message reaches Ella SMSC when the SMSC number on its SIM card is Ella SMSC's service centre address. The MME, SMSF or IP-SM-GW gives the phone's MSISDN, which is the sender. Ella SMSC converts the recipient to an international number with the operator's numbering plan, stores the message, and acknowledges it.

Applications send messages to phones with the [Messages API](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/messages/index.md), or over [SMPP](#esmes-over-smpp).

## Delivering

For each message, Ella SMSC asks the HSS for the serving nodes of the recipient, then tries them in turn until one takes the message. Messages to a phone go one at a time, in order. When more wait, the serving node that took one takes the next, without another routing lookup.

Each lookup and delivery is recorded as an attempt, shown in the UI and the API.

## When a phone is unreachable

When no serving node takes a message, Ella SMSC makes sure the HSS records that a message waits. The message and the recipient's other messages wait for a retry, after the [retry intervals](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/delivery/index.md). When the phone can receive messages again, the HSS alerts Ella SMSC, which delivers them right away.

A message ends:

- **delivered**, when a serving node takes it;
- **failed**, when the recipient is unknown, not allowed SMS, or has no serving node that supports SGd, when the SIM refuses a (U)SIM data download message, or when an attempt fails and the message is single-shot or retries are off;
- **expired**, when its validity period ends first;
- **replaced**, when a later message from the same sender replaces it. A message from the Messages API or an ESME is replaced only by one from the same user or ESME.

## Status reports

When a phone asks for status reports, Ella SMSC returns one to it when the message ends. It delivers the report as it does a message.

## ESMEs over SMPP

Platforms built for SMSCs, such as OTA platforms, connect as External Short Message Entities (ESMEs), over SMPP 3.4:

```
OTA platform (ESME) ──SMPP over TCP or TLS, 2775──▶ SMPP listener ──▶ submission ──▶ database ──▶ delivery ──▶ HSS, MME, SMSF
        ▲                                                                                       │
        └──────────────── deliver_sm: receipts, SIM answers ◀── notifications ◀─────────────────┘
```

- **The SMPP listener** accepts the ESMEs' connections, checks each bind against the ESME accounts, and keeps the sessions. An ESME account acts as a user: the messages it submits are that user's, and the user's role decides what it may do.
- **Submission.** Each `submit_sm` becomes one short message, through the same path as the [Messages API](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/messages/index.md), so the same parameters give the same message. Ella SMSC answers once the message is stored, then delivers it as any other.
- **Notifications.** When a message from an ESME ends, Ella SMSC queues the delivery receipt and the SIM's answer that the ESME asked for. It sends them as `deliver_sm` to a receiving session of that ESME, the answer first, and keeps them until the ESME acknowledges them, binds again, or they expire. They survive a restart.

See the [SMPP reference](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md).

## Binary messages

Applications can send binary messages, such as the (U)SIM data download messages that an OTA platform sends to update SIM cards: the phone passes them to the SIM instead of showing them. Ella SMSC delivers their parameters and user data unchanged, and keeps the phone's answer to each delivery attempt, which can carry the SIM's response.

# Security

## Users and roles

Everyone who uses the UI or the API is a user with a role: Admin, Read Only, Network Manager or Submitter. The role decides what the user can see and do, from reading settings to managing other users. See [Roles](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/#roles).

The first user, an Admin, is created when Ella SMSC is initialized. Admins create the others.

Ella SMSC limits login attempts, from each address and for each account, to slow down password guessing.

## Applications

Applications, such as an OTA platform, use an API token rather than a password. A token belongs to a user and has that user's role, but it cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users. Tokens can expire, and an Admin or the token's user can delete one at any time.

Give each application its own Submitter user: it can send messages, and read only the messages it sent.

## ESMEs

An ESME, such as an OTA platform, binds to the [SMPP listener](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md) with a `system_id` and a password. SMPP 3.4 limits that password to 8 characters, so Ella SMSC adds other checks:

- Each ESME acts as a user, whose role decides whether it may submit or receive.
- An ESME binds only from the networks in its allow-list. An empty list allows no address.
- Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes. A password the SMSC generates has 8 random letters and digits.
- Binds are limited from each address, and wrong passwords for each ESME. Every refused bind gets the same answer, so a client cannot tell which check failed.
- Only an Admin, logged in rather than with an API token, creates, changes or deletes ESMEs.

SMPP 3.4 has no encryption: the password and the messages cross the network in clear. TLS, with `smpp.tls`, is a common convention outside SMPP 3.4, which the ESME must support. Use plain TCP only over a private link, such as an IPsec VPN, or in a lab.

The allow-list checks the address of the TCP connection. Terminate TLS in Ella SMSC itself, not in a proxy or load balancer, which would hide the ESME's address. On Kubernetes, the Service keeps it with `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`.

## Message content

Messages carry personal content. Reading it is a permission of its own: a Read Only user sees that messages were sent and delivered, but not what they say. Every read of the content is recorded in an [audit event](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/observability/#audit-events), with who read it and from where.

## HTTPS

Ella SMSC serves the UI and the API over plain HTTP unless it is given a certificate in `api.tls` (see the [configuration file](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/config_file/index.md)). Use HTTPS whenever the UI or the API is reachable over a network you do not control.

## Diameter peers

Ella SMSC accepts any Diameter peer that connects and supports S6c or SGd, and its Diameter connections are not encrypted. Keep its Diameter address on a network that only the core network can reach.

Through an edge agent, other networks can send short messages to Ella SMSC, which does not filter them by realm. Have the edge agent accept only the operator's roaming partners.
